standard_prerequisites.name: Universal injectivity over a local base for a map whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is injective
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, labels lemma-universally-injective-local (proof line 2396) and lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian (proof line 2397)
standard_prerequisites.use: Together they show that the map from the free module to the localised module is universally injective over R once its reduction modulo the maximal ideal is injective, which is the heart of the implication (1) implies (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: Permanence and localisation of universal injectivity, and flatness of the cokernel of a universally injective map over a domain
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-universally-injective-permanence (proof line 2400), algebra-lemma-universally-injective-localize (proof line 2403) and algebra-lemma-ui-flat-domain (proof line 2405)
standard_prerequisites.use: Carries universal injectivity from the localised map back to the map on the local ring and makes the cokernel flat over R, which produces condition (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma, nonzerodivisors of a flat finitely presented ring map, and flatness of an extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-NAK (proof line 2411); Same chapter flat.tex, labels lemma-invert-universally-injective (proof line 2417) and lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian (proof line 2418); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-flat-ses (proof line 2421)
standard_prerequisites.use: Nakayama upgrades injectivity at p to an isomorphism, the nonzerodivisor statement lets injectivity at p be pulled back to injectivity at q, and flatness of an extension closes the cycle from (5) back to (1).

core_obligations: Construct alpha from a basis of the fibre: set r equal to the dimension of N tensor_S kappa(p) over kappa(p) and send the standard basis of the free module to elements of N forming such a basis; this gives the required S-module map (proof lines 2381-2386).

Prove the most interesting implication (1) implies (2): if N_q is R-flat, then since S/mS is a domain with fraction field kappa(p) the reduction of the free module modulo m maps injectively into N tensor_S kappa(p), so by the local universal injectivity criterion and the non Noetherian projectivity lemma the map S^{direct sum r} -> N_p is R-universally injective; by permanence of universal injectivity the map to N is universally injective, hence so is its localisation at q by the localisation statement, and therefore the cokernel at q is R-flat (proof lines 2388-2405).

Close the cycle of equivalences: (2) implies (3) immediately; if (3) holds then alpha at p is injective as a localisation, and Nakayama makes it surjective, so (3) implies (4); if (4) holds then alpha is injective because elements of S outside p are nonzerodivisors on S, so (4) implies (5); and if (5) holds then N_q is R-flat as an extension of flat modules, so (5) implies (1) (proof lines 2407-2422).
proof_roadmap: Build alpha from a basis of the fibre at p (proof lines 2381-2386).
Prove flatness at q implies universal injectivity of alpha with flat cokernel at q (proof lines 2388-2405).
Chain the remaining implications using Nakayama, nonzerodivisors and flatness of extensions (proof lines 2407-2422).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the algebraic induction step over a local base: for a finitely presented flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres and a finite module, it produces a map from a finite free module that is an isomorphism on the special fibre, and shows that flatness of the localisation at a prime over the maximal ideal is equivalent to four conditions involving universal injectivity of that map and flatness of its cokernel (statement lines 2355-2379, tag 05I3). The substantive part is the implication from flatness to universal injectivity, which needs the local universal injectivity criterion, the non Noetherian projectivity lemma, permanence and localisation of universal injectivity and flatness of the cokernel; the rest of the cycle is closed with Nakayama's lemma and a nonzerodivisor statement. The first implication is the substance, so the claim is H2.
